title: Coherent functors and transformations on common-stage pair categories
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $I=\mathsf{FinExt}_\ell$ be the small directed poset of finite intermediate fields [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set], using [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(\mathcal A_E,U_{F/E},a^A)$ and $(\mathcal B_E,V_{F/E},a^B)$ be diagrams of additive categories [def-weil-additive-category], with additive transition functors [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], identity transitions $U_{E/E}=1$ and $V_{E/E}=1$, and specified natural associator isomorphisms $a^A_{G,F,E}:U_{G/F}U_{F/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{G/E}$ and $a^B_{G,F,E}:V_{G/F}V_{F/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}V_{G/E}$ for $E\subseteq F\subseteq G$. Assume the associators with a repeated adjacent field are identities and the pentagon equations hold. Form their pair categories $P_A,P_B$: objects of $P_A$ are $(E,K)$ with $K\in\mathcal A_E$; morphisms from $(E,K)$ to $(F,L)$ are represented over $M\supseteq E,F$ by common-field maps $u:U_{M/E}K\to U_{M/F}L$, modulo equality after further transport $u_N=a^A_{N,M,F,L}U_{N/M}(u)(a^A_{N,M,E,K})^{-1}$, and likewise for $B$; identities, sums and composites are calculated at one common stage. These prescriptions are well-defined additive categories.

Let $\Phi_E:\mathcal A_E\to\mathcal B_E$ be additive functors with natural isomorphisms
$$b_{F/E}:V_{F/E}\Phi_E\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi_F U_{F/E}.$$
Assume $b_{E/E}=1$ and the tower equation
$$b_{G/E}\circ(a^B_{G,F,E}\Phi_E)=(\Phi_G a^A_{G,F,E})\circ(b_{G/F}U_{F/E})\circ(V_{G/F}b_{F/E}).$$
Then the formulas
$$\Phi(E,K)=(E,\Phi_EK),\qquad
 \Phi[M,u]=[M,b_{M/F,L}^{-1}\circ\Phi_M(u)\circ b_{M/E,K}]
$$
define an additive functor $P_A\to P_B$, independent of the representative and common field. If $\Psi_E$ is another such family with comparisons $c$, and natural transformations $\eta_E:\Phi_E\Rightarrow\Psi_E$ satisfy
$$\eta_F U_{F/E}\circ b_{F/E}=c_{F/E}\circ V_{F/E}\eta_E,$$
then the components $[E,\eta_{E,K}]$ give a natural transformation $\Phi\Rightarrow\Psi$. Identities, composition of functor families with the composite comparisons, and equations of compatible transformations are preserved by this construction. The descended functors and transformations extend to $\Kar(P_A)\to\Kar(P_B)$ [def-weil-karoubi-envelope]: a functor sends $(P,p)$ to $(\Phi P,\Phi p)$ and a transformation has component $\Psi(p)\eta_P\Phi(p)$.
